1. Scope

  • All 107 baseline transcripts (baseline/transcripts): 76 LINK/COMMAREA transcripts replayed on legacy via the GnuCOBOL harness and on the migrated service via the REST API of docs/migration/api-contract.md; 31 terminal-mode (BNKMENU/BNK1*) transcripts replayed through the migrated 3270 screen handlers.
  • 5 API variants: every DBCRFUN teller transcript re-run through PUT /banking/account/{debit|credit}/{id}.
  • 6 multi-step user journeys (parity/flows/user-flows.json), compared after every step.
  • 7 React read endpoints on the Liberty layer cross-checked against the same query on the legacy seeded DB.
  • Per flow: outcome (success / fail code / ABEND code), every business response field, DB delta of CUSTOMER, ACCOUNT, PROCTRAN, CONTROL and the full table dumps after the flow (PROCTRAN_REF included).
  • The whole flow set runs twice: migrated side on H2 (default profile) and on PostgreSQL (profile postgres); the legacy side is re-run for each flow in both passes.
  • React: unit tests (react-scripts/Jest), production build, and the built UI served by the migrated service driven in headless Chromium against each database (section 6).

5. MIGRATION DEFECTS

No migration defect observed on H2 or PostgreSQL.

Harness findings in this round (parity/** only)

  • First PostgreSQL run: CREACC/max-accounts and CREACC/ninth-account ended in ERROR before comparison because the harness translated their SQLite setup_sql (recursive CTE) to H2-only SYSTEM_RANGE; the migrated service correctly returned 500 for that statement. Fixed in parity/tools/parity.py (sqlite_to_migrated: generate_series on PostgreSQL). Both flows MATCH on PostgreSQL after the fix. Harness defect, not a migration defect.
  • PostgreSQL folds the unquoted legacy column names of the in-process 3270 dumps to lower case; parity/tools/ScreenParity.java upper-cases dump keys so the CUSTOMER/ACCOUNT/PROCTRAN/CONTROL dumps compare column by column.

7. KNOWN LIMITATIONS (coverage boundaries; no flow difference is attributed to them)

  • Legacy ran under GnuCOBOL 3.1.2 + the C/SQLite CICS/DB2/VSAM stub runtime (legacy/), not on z/OS CICS/DB2/VSAM. Parity is against that harness (107/107 baseline transcripts replay with no golden fixtures).
  • The migrated side is driven through a parity-only test seam (parity/tools/ParityServer.java: /__parity reset, EIBTASKN restart, exec, dump); all business beans are the unmodified target/classes. ABNDPROC/record uses the property-gated, token-protected POST/GET /banking/admin/abend, enabled only on the parity server (disabled by default).
  • BANKDATA (batch) is not replayed per flow: its output is the canonical seed, and the seeded CUSTOMER/ACCOUNT/PROCTRAN/CONTROL dumps of both sides were verified identical before every flow on both databases.
  • 3270 screen flows (BNKMENU/BNK1*) have no REST surface: they run in-process through the com.ibm.cics.cip.bank.core.screens handlers (parity/tools/ScreenParity.java). Screen fields and table dumps are compared; RETURN COMMAREA bytes are not (Java keeps a symbolic state map).
  • React UI in Chromium covers the read paths (customer by number, accounts of a customer, name search, account by number) on both databases. Create/update/delete screens were not driven in the browser in this round; their REST calls are covered by the API flows and by the React axios contract tests. (PR #26 reported a browser CRUD run on PostgreSQL; not re-observed here.)
  • Pre-existing UI quirk (production React source, unchanged): CustomerDetailsPage Submit toggles table visibility, so a consecutive search needs a second Submit.
  • PostgreSQL: flows run serially, one fresh schema per parity server (DROP/CREATE before start); concurrency on PostgreSQL is covered only by the opt-in PostgresProfileMainFlowsTest (concurrent counter allocation).
  • Comparison normalisation: CHAR right-trim, numbers to 2dp, row order. Nothing else is masked; PROCTRAN_REF and every other column is compared.

RefDefectFlows exercising itParity status
README #1Abend time HH:MM:MM - the ABND-TIME STRING concatenates WS-TIME-NOW-GRP-MM twice instead of minutes then seconds. Present in 23 programs (all BNK1*, BNKMENU, CRDTAGY1-5, CREACC, CRECUST, DBCRFUN, DELACC, DELCUS, INQACC, INQACCCU, INQCUST, XFRFUN). Found by reading the source; no recorded flow reaches those abend paths.ABNDPROC/recordevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #2DBCRFUN ignores the overdraft limit - a payment-interface debit (COMM-FACILTYPE = 496) fails with code 3 whenever available balance + amount < 0, even inside the overdraft (DBCRFUN/within-overdraft: balance 0, limit 500, debit 400 -> refused).DBCRFUN/credit-payment-api, DBCRFUN/debit-payment-api, DBCRFUN/loan-payment-api, DBCRFUN/mortgage-payment-api, DBCRFUN/within-overdraftevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #3Teller debits have no funds check - with any FACILTYPE other than 496 a debit can drive any account negative (DBCRFUN/insufficient-funds-teller, BNK1CRA/debit-insufficient).DBCRFUN/credit-teller, TELLER-REST/credit-teller, DBCRFUN/debit-teller, TELLER-REST/debit-teller, DBCRFUN/insufficient-funds-teller, TELLER-REST/insufficient-funds-teller, DBCRFUN/loan-teller, TELLER-REST/loan-teller, TELLER-REST/not-foundevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #4LOAN/MORTGAGE - only payment-interface requests are refused (fail code 4); teller credits/debits are applied (DBCRFUN/loan-teller).DBCRFUN/loan-payment-api, DBCRFUN/loan-teller, TELLER-REST/loan-teller, DBCRFUN/mortgage-payment-apievery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL

README #7XFRFUN same account abends the task with SAME instead of returning a fail code.XFRFUN/same-accountevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #8XFRFUN to-account not found returns fail code 2 after two SYNCPOINT ROLLBACKs.XFRFUN/to-not-foundevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #9UPDACC does not validate the account type - CHEQUE is written (UPDACC/invalid-type); only a blank type is rejected. Balances in the COMMAREA are ignored.UPDACC/invalid-typeevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #10UPDCUST only updates name/address; DOB and credit score in the COMMAREA are ignored. A blank name keeps the old name.UPDCUST/ignores-dob-and-scoreevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #11BNK1DCS non-numeric customer number - BIF DEEDIT turns ABC into 0000000000, which INQCUST treats as "random customer", so the screen shows a random customer with "Customer lookup successful.".BNK1DCS/lookup-non-numericevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #12BNK1CAC overdraft length underflow - SUBTRACT <trailing blanks> FROM OVERDRL assumes the field is transmitted with its trailing blanks. If a terminal sends a short field (e.g. 0 with L=1) OVERDRL goes negative and INSPECT OVERDRI(1:OVERDRL) is an invalid reference modification (GnuCOBOL runtime crash; undefined on z/OS without SSRANGE). Screen transcripts therefore send fields blank-padded to their full width, as a 3270 does for a field pre-filled with blanks.BNK1CAC/create-ok, BNK1CAC/first-display, BNK1CAC/invalid-typeevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #13BANKDATA account data - with 1,30,1,42 it creates no MORTGAGE accounts; LAST/NEXT statement dates are fixed literals; CURRENT overdraft limit is always 100.-no flow exercises it directly (BANKDATA output = canonical seed, verified identical before every flow)
README #14CRECUST review date and BANKDATA use FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (the real system clock), not CICS time - the only wall-clock dependency in the estate; the harness pins it via COB_CURRENT_DATE.CRECUST/ok-seed-1234-taskn-500, CRECUST/ok-seed-42, CRECUST/ok-seed-7every flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #15Credit scores depend on the CICS task number (RANDOM(EIBTASKN)), so on a real region two identical requests get different scores.CRECUST/ok-seed-1234-taskn-500every flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #16Typo in DELCUS abend free-form text: "Unbale to DELETE CUSTOMER VSAM rec".-not exercised: no transcript forces the DELCUS VSAM-delete failure that writes this abend text
README #17INQACCCU returns success with 0 accounts for an existing customer without accounts, but fail code 1 for a non-existent customer.INQACCCU/customer-not-found, INQACCCU/no-accountsevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
README #18CREACC rejects lower-case types (isa, fail code A); the 10th account is refused with fail code 8 (> 9 accounts check), the 9th is allowed.CREACC/lowercase-type, CREACC/max-accounts, CREACC/ninth-accountevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
new in round 2INQCUST custno 0 ("random customer") always returns customer 0000000001 under the harness, whatever CBSA_RANDOM_SEED (GnuCOBOL -std=ibm COMPUTE truncation of RANDOM(EIBTASKN)); BNK1DCS non-numeric input inherits it.INQCUST/random-seed-42, INQCUST/random-seed-7, BNK1DCS/lookup-non-numericevery flow exercising it is identical (legacy behaviour reproduced) on H2 and PostgreSQL
